html:
The Shawi, also called Chayahuita, are an Indigenous people of the Amazon lowlands of northern Peru, in the Loreto region along the Paranapura and Cahuapanas rivers near Yurimaguas.

Their language belongs to the small Cahuapanan family, whose only other member is Shiwilu (Jebero). Jesuit missions from Quito reached the area in the 1600s. The Shawi live by farming manioc and plantains, fishing and hunting. Their neighbours include the Awajún and the Kandozi.
